open-question.question: Which conflicting decision stands: "Installed copies for suite" or "Plugin copy running mission"? "Installed copies for suite" has the maintainer bring each host's installed copy to the renamed build before the suite runs, with the host's documented install as CONTRIBUTING.md states it, which for Claude Code is a directory marketplace on this checkout with the plugin installed at a scope outside any project, so from then on every session on the machine loads the renamed plugin from the working tree's hosts/claude. "Plugin copy running mission" says nothing loads from the working tree's hosts/ during the mission, and that the marketplace is added from the working tree's hosts/claude under the name gurita only after the finish. The suite runs before the release, and the release before the finish.
open-question.recommendation: The frozen copy keeps running every task, the release, and the finish, and the suite gets the documented directory-marketplace install its prerequisite line names; the two plugins differ in name and namespace, so they load side by side, and a snapshot checkout would add upkeep to protect a copy the mission never runs.
open-question.alternative: Both entries stand, and "Plugin copy running mission" gains one stated exception. From the maintainer's suite install on, gurita@gurita is installed at user scope from the directory marketplace on this checkout and loads from the working tree's hosts/claude in every session, beside the frozen cairn copy. Every task and the finish are still invoked through cairn: from the frozen copy. The renamed install stays in place, so the closing step after the finish shrinks to dropping the stale cairn copy, with nothing left to re-add. It is the smallest change to the record. The suite gets its documented install, and the frozen copy still runs everything the mission does, because the two plugins have different names and namespaces and do not clash. "Nothing loads from the working tree" stops being true for the last stretch of the mission. Sessions see two full skill sets that differ only in namespace, so the wrong one can be picked by routing or by hand. Any rebuild after the install, the release commit's 2.0.0 manifests included, changes what the gurita copy serves while a session runs.

alternative.id: Switch to live gurita at install

open-question.alternative: "Installed copies for suite" stands as written, and "Plugin copy running mission" is rewritten to end at that install. Before the suite task, the maintainer installs gurita@gurita at user scope from the directory marketplace on this checkout, as CONTRIBUTING.md documents it. At the same point the frozen cairn marketplace and its install are dropped, so the suite task, the release task, and the finish run under the renamed plugin loaded from the working tree's hosts/claude and are invoked as /gurita:<skill>. The frozen entry's closing step, re-adding the marketplace under gurita after the finish, is deleted because the install has already done it. The suite's Claude Code check is met exactly as the host suite and CONTRIBUTING.md describe it: a readFromFolder install where the comparison with hosts/claude passes trivially. The release and the finish also become the renamed plugin's first real runs, before the 2.0.0 tag is published. The last three steps run from the tree they change. The release commit rebuilds the host manifests at 2.0.0 while its own session is using them, and the protection the frozen copy was chosen for is gone exactly when the maintainer runs /release-plugin and finish-mission. Tasks entered before the switch name cairn: invocations that are no longer installed.

alternative.id: Live install only around suite runs

open-question.alternative: "Plugin copy running mission" stands. "Installed copies for suite" is narrowed to a window: the maintainer installs gurita@gurita at user scope from the directory marketplace on this checkout directly before the suite task and uninstalls it once the release pre-flight's suite run has passed. Throughout, the frozen cairn copy runs every task and the finish. The re-add under gurita after the finish happens as already written. The frozen entry's promise and its post-finish step stay intact. The live-tree copy loads only while the two suite runs need it, and the suite still sees the documented directory-marketplace install. The window ends inside the release task, between its pre-flight and its publish, so the maintainer has an uninstall to do by hand mid-release, and the "Release run actor" decision does not provide for it. If the uninstall is forgotten, the second option's state is left standing without being recorded. Between the install and the uninstall, any session started on the machine still loads the live tree.

"Plugin copy running mission" stands. "Installed copies for suite" is rewritten for Claude Code only: the maintainer installs gurita@gurita at user scope from a directory marketplace on a separate checkout or worktree. That checkout is held at the commit the suite task runs on, and its hosts/claude equals the working tree's built tree there. Nothing is installed from this checkout's own hosts/claude. That snapshot install stays until the post-finish step replaces it with the marketplace on the working tree, as the frozen entry already says. Antigravity and Codex installs are unchanged. Nothing loads from the working tree at any point in the mission, and the suite still finds a user-scope gurita copy that equals the built tree. Both entries keep their purpose, and the host suite needs no change. A third checkout has to be managed, and it must be moved again if anything under hosts/claude changes between the suite task and the release pre-flight. Otherwise the pre-flight's comparison fails. Every session still loads a second, gurita-named skill set beside the frozen cairn copy. CONTRIBUTING.md's install instructions are followed only loosely, since they point at a checkout of the source rather than a snapshot of it.

This option rejects the premise that the Claude Code suite needs a machine-wide install. "Plugin copy running mission" stands. "Installed copies for suite" is rewritten so that nothing is installed for Claude Code. Instead, a task ordered before the suite task changes host_tests so that each headless claude process loads the built hosts/claude for that process only, through a session-level plugin-directory mechanism of this host, and the user-scope install check is replaced. CONTRIBUTING.md's description of the suite changes to match. Antigravity and Codex keep their documented installs. The conflict goes away for good: no session outside the suite ever loads the renamed tree, the frozen copy's promise holds with no exception, and later missions can run the Claude Code suite without touching the machine's install. It redesigns the host suite inside a rename mission, on a host mechanism no hands-on check has tested yet. It adds a trigger-set change, and the "Host suite timing" order has to put that change ahead of the suite task. The new form also drops the suite's guarantee that it exercises the copy the host actually installs, which the "Hands-on check blocks" re-check of the install point rests on.

open-question.question: When does the tracked .claude/settings.json stop enabling cairn@cairn and enable gurita@gurita instead? That entry is this checkout's one recorded install of the plugin, at project scope, and by decision a copy frozen under the name cairn runs every task of this mission and its finish. A task that rewrites the entry takes the frozen copy away from every session started after it, the release task's and the finish's included; leaving the entry as it is leaves an old-name identifier that the closing whole-tree search finds, that no decision keeps, and that the 2.0.0 tag records.

recommendation.option: Keep through release, remove after finish

open-question.recommendation: The entry is what loads the frozen copy, so it stays untouched until the finish has used it, and it is then deleted, not renamed, because the commit that added it on 2026-11-18 called it temporary and the file enabled no copy of the plugin before it.

alternative.id: Keep through release, remove after finish

open-question.alternative: No task of this mission touches `.claude/settings.json`. The `cairn@cairn` entry stands through the release and the finish, so the frozen copy keeps loading with no further step. After the finish, the maintainer deletes the entry in a hand commit outside the mission, returning the file to its pre-`0a823b7` state, and enables `gurita@gurita` out of tree (the git-ignored `.claude/settings.local.json` or user scope) when the marketplace is re-added under the name gurita. The closing search's residue list names `.claude/settings.json`, count 1, kept by this decision until after the finish. The mission runs on the install that works today with no added risk, and after the finish the tracked tree carries no machine-specific install identifier under either name. A later marketplace change never has to touch the file. The 2.0.0 tag still records `cairn@cairn`, an old-name identifier in the released source. After the finish a checkout no longer enables the plugin for the project, and both the deletion and the out-of-tree enablement are hand steps outside the mission that nothing records or checks.

alternative.id: Rewrite before release, enable frozen copy locally

open-question.alternative: A task of this mission, ordered before the release task, rewrites the tracked `.claude/settings.json` entry from `cairn@cairn` to `gurita@gurita`. Before that task's change reaches any later session, the maintainer enables the frozen copy for this checkout outside the tracked tree, as `cairn@cairn` in the git-ignored `.claude/settings.local.json` or at user scope, by hand, outside the task list. After the finish the maintainer drops that out-of-tree `cairn@cairn` enablement when the marketplace is re-added under the name gurita. The closing whole-tree search finds nothing in the file, and the 2.0.0 tag records `gurita@gurita`. The released source records the plugin under its new name only. A checkout of the 2.0.0 tag enables exactly what the renamed CONTRIBUTING.md tells a contributor to install, and the closing search needs no residue entry for the file, while the frozen copy keeps running every later task, the release, and the finish. It adds one more machine-level step to the maintainer's setup, one no commit records and the run never checks. From the rewrite until after the finish, every session enables `gurita@gurita` while the machine has no gurita marketplace for it, unless the renamed copy is installed earlier. Whether that happens depends on how the sibling conflict over installing the renamed copies for the host suite is settled. If the local enablement is forgotten, the first session after the rewrite starts without the plugin, and so the release task's `/submit-task` and `/complete-task` and the finish are lost.

alternative.id: Remove before release, enable both out of tree

open-question.alternative: A task of this mission, ordered before the release task, deletes the `cairn@cairn` line from the tracked `.claude/settings.json` and adds nothing in its place. This returns the file to its state before `0a823b7` ("plugin repointed temporarily", 2026-11-18), when it enabled only `skill-creator@claude-plugins-official`. Before that task's change reaches any later session, the maintainer enables the frozen copy for this checkout outside the tracked tree (the git-ignored `.claude/settings.local.json` or user scope), by hand. The tracked tree stops carrying a machine-specific install identifier under either name, undoing an entry its own commit called temporary. No session ever enables a plugin whose marketplace is missing, and no later rename or marketplace change has to touch the file again. A checkout of the tag, or a fresh clone, no longer enables the plugin for the project, so a contributor's session loads it only if they enable it themselves. Both the frozen copy's enablement and the post-finish `gurita@gurita` enablement become hand steps that no commit records. If the first is forgotten, every session after the removal starts without the plugin, and so the release and the finish are lost.

alternative.id: Rewrite as last task, finish in running session

open-question.alternative: The last task of the list `derive-tasks` writes rewrites the tracked entry from `cairn@cairn` to `gurita@gurita`, and nothing enables the frozen copy anywhere else. The maintainer enters and completes the release task, then runs the finish, in the session that ran `complete-all-tasks`. That session started before the rewrite, so it keeps the frozen copy it loaded at startup. The closing search finds nothing in the file, and the 2.0.0 tag records `gurita@gurita`. It needs no out-of-tree enablement and no hand step beyond those already decided. The tag records only the new name, and the rewrite is an ordinary task commit inside the mission.
